question:
In the following decomposition reaction, identify the p q r s:

p feSO₄ (s) → q fe₂o₃ (s) + r SO₂ (g) + s SO₃ (g)
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4: 2,1,1,1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The decomposition of iron(II) sulfate heptahydrate (FeSO₄) occurs when heated, producing ferric oxide (Fe₂O₃), sulfur dioxide (SO₂), and sulfur trioxide (SO₃).
 
• The balanced chemical equation is: **2 FeSO₄(s) → Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g)**.
 
• The coefficients p, q, r, and s in the equation are determined based on stoichiometric balance: p = 2, q = 1, r = 1, s = 1.
 
• Option 4 correctly matches the stoichiometric coefficients: p = 2, q = 1, r = 1, s = 1.
 
• This reaction is an example of a thermal decomposition reaction, where heat causes the compound to break down into simpler substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thermal Decomposition Reaction:**

 
 
• It is a chemical reaction in which a compound breaks down into simpler substances when heated.
 
• Common examples include the decomposition of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) into calcium oxide (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂).
 
 
 
• **Iron Compounds in Chemistry:**
 
 
• Iron exists in multiple oxidation states, commonly +2 (ferrous) and +3 (ferric).
 
• FeSO₄ (ferrous sulfate) is often used in industrial processes and as a precursor in various reactions.
 
 
 
• **Sulfur Oxides:**
 
 
• SO₂ (sulfur dioxide) and SO₃ (sulfur trioxide) are important industrial chemicals.
 
• SO₂ is a precursor to sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) production via the contact process.
 
 
 
• **Stoichiometry:**
 
 
• Stoichiometry involves the calculation of reactants and products in chemical reactions based on balanced equations.
 
• It ensures the conservation of mass and the correct molar ratios in reactions.
